Deep learning techniques have become instrumental in various vision tasks; however, in domains like industrial defect detection, it is often impractical to secure abundant annotated samples for every specific category. Address this challenge, we propose a novel framework termed Few-Sample Learning (FSL) with Prototype Learning (PL). In PL, each category is represented by a prototype that captures the type-based characteristics of that category. Furthermore, we designed a prototype learning network to derive category-specific prototypes from existing teacher instances. These teacher instances are initial support samples provided for each category in an FSL setting. Using these prototypes, the classification criteria are shifted from calculating affinity with multiple support samples to assessing affinity against a single prototype per category. Consequently, this network can generalize its abilities to novel categories even with minimal sample counts. We conducted comprehensive experiments across two real-world industrial defect detection benchmarks, where we supplied only 10 images per novel category. Results indicate that our approach achieves a mean Hamming accuracy of 13.0% higher than the baseline, outperforming advanced teacher-learning based methods by an additional 33% in the specified defect detection benchmark.

Conventional soundproofing methods rely on traditional resonators, but their large size relative to acoustic wavelengths hinders their compactness. Overcoming this limitation, microacoustic metagratings composed of sub-wavelength acoustic dipoles have demonstrated effectiveness at reducing the resonance threshold while maintaining high sound insulation; however, these structures have yet to be realized at the microscale. In this paper, we present a acoustic metagrating designed at the microscale, created using two-photon lithography within a flexible polyurethane (TPU) elastic polymer. Acoustic energy above a 500 Hz wavelength impinged upon this device generates opposing dipoles that form below 250 Hz, successfully achieving sound attenuation exceeding 30 dB at frequencies above 200 Hz. Although the elastic properties differ among the materials used for the traditional methods compared to our fabricated one, the resulting sound dipoles allow for soundproofing at ultra-high frequencies not achievable by prior metagratings. This proof-of-concept indicates the fabrication capability of acoustic metagrates using TPU via two-photon lithography, enabling soundproofing at frequencies up into the ultrasonic range. This paves an avenue for acoustic engineering at the microscale in applications involving small devices and living organisms.

Anomalous diffusion, characterized by deviations from standard Brownian motion in both regimes of super-diffusion (faster than Brownian) and sub-diffusion (slower than Brownian), is extensively observed in biological systems. Consequently, understanding effective dynamics becomes inextricably linked to analyzing drift and effective potentials derived from full two-dimensional probability density functions (PDFs).

Conversely, the turnover visible in lower-mass galaxies aligns with non-gritational feedback mechanisms. Additionally, we detect that both the maturity and spatial extent of the potential associated with bulges differ markedly between samples, suggesting these factors critically dictate both structural and stellar evolutionary histories in massive systems.

Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) aims to discover textual descriptions of visual interactions between objects. Existing methods struggle with errors, as models often predict erroneous object pairs—pairs of objects that do not perform the stated action—more frequently than correct ones. These errors can be grouped into implicit and explicit categories. Implicit erroneous object pairs arise when there is insufficient evidence to support them, whereas explicit erroneous pairs result from strong confidence in incorrect predictions, often due to ambiguous or conflicting cues in the input image (for example, similar visual features suggesting another possible pair, or parts of an individual object being mistaken for a second object). To address these challenges, this study focuses explicitly on explicit erroneous predictions. Our strategy involves first identifying ambiguous or conflicting cues responsible for such errors and then separating implicit information from explicit information within ambiguous regions to construct disambiguation signals effective at reducing erroneous detections. Empirical results demonstrate that leveraging disambiguation signals helps resolve explicit erroneous object pairs, yielding notable improvements in recall@K and the customized Human Evaluation metric.

Encoded logical qubits in the toric code demonstrate intrinsic resilience against random hardware faults, making them an attractive platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation where several types of universal gate sets can operate with only modest overhead. Multivariate point processes are extensively used to analyze temporal events across various domains, such as neural activity, asset trades, and communication transactions. These processes often incorporate nonlinear specifications to capture intricate patterns; however, these complexities typically hinder statistical description and inference. Although maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) can achieve consistent results, it fails to provide full posterior distributions, which contain richer probabilistic insights. In this study, we propose a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methodology for the Bayesian inference of nonlinear Hawkes processes. Our approach involves constructing an auxiliary Metropolis-Hastings algorithm that integrates stochastic integrals using quasi-Gaussian samples, enabling full posterior inference even in scenarios where standard Monte Carlo integration is infeasible. Simulation results indicate that the proposed Bayesian estimator is consistent and outperforms traditional MLE techniques in both estimation accuracy and ranking performance. Finally, we examine a real-world example using an International Futures Input-Output model to highlight the practical applicability of the suggested framework.

Chirped multi-wiggle-plasma lenses (CPALs) function as an enduring challenge for high-intensity laser technology. Although generating these lenses in highly magnetized, thin, and chirped gasemine targets is anticipated, significant obstacles persist in achieving the necessary peak intensities (>10²⁰ to 10²¹ W/cm³) required for applications like photon acceleration, neutron generation, and plasma fusion. This study reveals that CPALs with peaks intensities exceeding 10²⁰ W/cm³ can indeed be generated using a 3.5 J, 0.75-fs optical cycle laser pulse with a 20-Tesla magnetic field gradient of 10¹¹ T/m. This approach involves interacting a pulse one optical cycle long with such a field-overwhelming structure that the magnetic force dominates electron dynamics, decoupling them from plasma. We employ the term "field-overwhelming" to describe interactions where external magnetic forces dictate motion. This setup produces plasma lensing effects through combined radiation pressure and forced electron oscillations, resulting in cone-shaped accelerated plasma jets with peaks intensities exceeding 10²⁰ W/cm³.

An investigation into possible variations of the tau lepton's electric dipole moment (EDM) faces significant obstacles. First, theoretical predictions for both its magnetic anomaly and EDM, which could indicate physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM), are severely constrained by large theoretical uncertainties stemming from quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Second, experimental data faces bulky systematic errors, leaving an eight sigma standard deviation gap between observations and SM predictions for the EDM component. This work outlines strategies to mitigate both uncertainties through enhanced lattice QCD calculations and refined measurements of tau polarization at particle accelerators.

The analysis supports the practical feasibility of employing the enhanced decoder with RBMRE codes to achieve minimum distance decodable performance even in scenarios involving noisy basis A, although such a combination was somewhat implicit in prior applications. To substantiate these theoretical findings, simulation outcomes are supplied.

We verify our building blocks against existing literature examples, successfully reproduishing recent findings by Guzen and others, and offer a streamlined derivation that improves upon earlier methods.

Folding CMB delensing techniques with state-of-the-art nonparametric reconstruction holds the promise of pushing precision cosmology limits and future experiments one step closer. This study examines the feasibility of reconstructing lensing potentials using generative models and enhancing delensing efficiency when primordial tensor modes are present. To achieve this, we proposed a novel neural network architecture that promises more efficient reconstruction by incorporating constraints on the three-dimensional matter distribution. Specifically, unlike standard methods, our approach utilizes only HEALPix gridded temperature and polarization data to simultaneously reconstruct potential realizations and estimate their power spectra. We evaluated the method's performance during linear and $25 h^{-1} \text{Gpc}^3$ simulations, analyzing reconstructions from two networks with different training goals: one targeting standard single potential estimation, and another targeting multiple potential realizations alongside power spectrum calculations. Our multi-potential network demonstrated superior robustness against tensor modes, particularly in larger matter simulations, and yielded more accurate estimated power spectra. Crucially, when estimating the amplitude of tensor perturbations with the multi-potential network in a simulation matching the complexity of real sky data ($25 h^{-1} \text{Gpc}^3$), biases dropped to $10^{-4}$—a significant improvement over the single-potential network, which showed approximately $10^{-3}$ reduction. In 1992, Gelfand and MacPherson derived an algebraic expression for Pontrjagin classes within the Algebras of Rational Functions field (ARF), revealing a link to Grobner bases, and originally introduced the result using arrangements of hyperplanes. This article offers alternative algebraic derivations of the formula, employing Grobner bases methods alongside observations on elementary symmetric functions within noncommutative algebras. Additionally, this work presents a generalization of the Gelfand-MacPherson formula to the context of Grothendieck-Bernstein topological enumerative formulas.

This paper details the timely optical spectroscopic monitoring of SN~2020jfo, a Type~{II} supernova identified by the SV-NS collaboration during a secure spectroscopic survey. Based on six post-peak spectra tracked between 0.68 and 18.26 days, our analysis reveals a relatively short plateau duration ($t_{\rm plateau}=23.45\,{\rm d}$) alongside outward expansion velocitiesexceeding those typically associated with this class ($\sim 10,000\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). While the initial spectra indicate an intermediate I classification, the supernova transitioned to Type II during the later observation period. Leveraging light curve shape analysis, photometric data from multiple sources, and refined spectroscopic measurements, we synthesized a comprehensive model excluding external factors like circumstellar interaction or stellar kicks. Instead, the discrepancies arising from observations versus the reduced one-dimensional symmetric model are explained by the presence of merger-induced asymmetry; the underlying bilobe structure, unstable due to radiation pressure, undergoes oscillation, which effectively manifests as the unusual features seen in SN~{}through a fitting process.

We investigate the use of multiplexed lobster-eye lenses as a method for X-ray telemetry. This approach combines multiple circular lobster-eye lenses, each employing microreplicas with circular ridge structures to form an image through photon reflection and statistical aggregation of path lengths. Our analysis focuses on designing a system capable of telemetry for Sun-like stars, requiring a 1° field of view, 1 keval energy range, and 1 arcsecond angular resolution. Using a lens design derived from recent laboratory findings by Sirono et al. (2020), we describe a configured array of 3.5-meter diameter lenses arranged on a square grid with 2.8-meter spacing. Simulation outcomes show this arrangement successfully records X-ray data for Sun-like stars within the specified field and energy ranges, achieving angular resolutions and sensitivities comparable to those of current state-of-the-long X-ray telescopes. Introducing this lens-type array could significantly simplify the feasibility of X-ray telemetry via lobster-eye architectures.

The development of massive dark matter halos is significantly influenced by both background cosmological conditions and foreground velocity structures, the latter often neglected in prior research yet instrumental in modifying the dark matter matter concentration within such halos in various ways. By training a neural network to predict halo mass at fixed redshifts from particle data, we demonstrate that the model implicitly identifies and utilizes multiple indicators of the vortex nature, disorder (velocity gradient), average flow orientation relative to the host halo, and fluctuations in the velocity field around it. Furthermore, analysis of the input importance suggests interactions governing how these descriptors influence halo growth vary depending on both redshift and field strength; specifically, the algorithm detects intricate connections between the velocity gradient and chaos levels together with proximity to large structures (clusters or voids). Ultimately, our results highlight that the velocity field around major structures possesses a complex influence on their formation which cannot be simplified or summarized by isolated descriptors.

Automatic Music Transcription converts audio recordings into symbolic music notation, serving as a vital music analysis tool. Although significant progress has been made, the field still struggles with low accuracy in music transcription and a reliance on extensive annotated datasets for training. To mitigate these issues, this study introduces a new, lightweight architecture designed specifically for keyboard transcription that integrates automatic transcription with semi-supervised learning. In this setup, only a small subset of labeled data is required for training. The system employs Convolutive Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (CNMF) to learn latent keyboard generative models from both labeled and unlabeled data, ensuring the model remains simple and efficient. Specifically, only a few annotated recordings are used to train the dictionary, which is then applied to label the transcription of the corresponding signals. Evaluation on two datasets demonstrates that this method achieves state-of-the-art transcription accuracy using a dataset size roughly 40 times smaller than standard requirements, with implementation being straightforward and the resulting code available on GitHub (https://github.com/mayberrr/SSKTE-CNNNMF).

We introduce a novel formulation for algebraically formulating the equilibrium configurations of rotating stars within general relativity. Currently, these states are defined by a set of coupled, non-linear differential equations derived from the Einstein field equations using a $(\text{cylindrical } r, \phi, z)$ coordinate system aligned with the axis of symmetry. This new approach achieves an invariant coordinate system through expressed expressions of physical variables, decouples these equations, and reformulates them as a system suitable for integration along specific curves defined by constant cylindrical radii. The reduction of this coupled system yields exactly five integral constants; however, due to the nature of the new integral formulation and four initial boundary conditions inherent in its history, only two are actually inertial-independent. To demonstrate the framework, we incorporate Tolsa and Krsak's models by rewriting them within this revised formal.

Exposing deep learning models for visual document extraction with high-quality labeled analogs to identical items is currently prohibitively costly due to the intricate nature of visual labeling and the vast volume of required unlabeled reference "barcodes." To solve this, we substitute traditional one-to-one labeling of both query and alternative labels as a method. By leveraging the community-wide availability of many alternatives for any given inquiry label, we facilitate more economical labeling while simultaneously offering the model richer contextual support through data abundance. We introduce "barcoding," which utilizes these inquiry/barcode pairings to supply models not only with richer informational context but also significant quantity. Investigation into how various constituent elements influence performance on inquiry barcodes shows that this method effectively mitigates the costs associated with costly data labeling, provides more robust data volume compensation, and yields superior performance compared to single isolated labels or a multitude of individual data bars.

The rate in which Neutron Star-Black Hole (NSBH) Gravitational Waves (GWs) are generated is anticianted to surpass that of other GW sources arising from compact object mergers. Although current GW detectors operated by LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA are capable of observing these waves, the primary challenge lies in identifying them. This difficulty stems from both computational constraints and potential losses in signal-to-noise content. This research leverages General Relativity to simulate NSBH merger scenarios, utilizing data on neutron star equations of state (EOS) and black hole spin parameters (NSBHGR). We employed LIGO's sensitivities (LIGO-V5) and developed Interferential Filters (IF) optimized for these detectors using F-filter techniques. Subsequently, we trained the Residual Neural Network (RNN) via ResNet architecture using a comprehensive dataset of general-residue neural networks to classify sources based on their properties, achieving near 99.99% precision for GW frequency discrimination from NSBH mergers. This approach paves a way for future studies of these events.

Health and overall well-being are significantly influenced by extrinsic, controllable elements known as social determinants (SDH) or the social environment. As a major software engineering research direction, there is currently a lack of sufficient attention to the automatic extraction of these factors from the web. This work establishes a web-based, marker-driven framework designed to identify social determinants of the external world. The approach utilizes three specific language marker domains: professional licensing, job advertisements, and personal web profiles (such as LinkedIn). The underlying architecture relies on sequence-to-sequence neural networks operating within a sophisticated training framework designed to manage various linguistic structures. Evaluations utilizing (LinkedIn) data demonstrate the effective recognition of social determinants encompassing professional licenses, job requirements, and biographical profiles generated by the model. These social determinants prove valuable in assessing and predicting career trajectories, hiring outcomes, and general life progress. Furthermore, these capabilities offer a pathway to create web services that provide external support, hiring tools, and counseling. Beyond this specific application, the study confirms that successfully capturing context-dependent features is vital for addressing tasks inherent in life-domain modeling.

This paper has re-examered the sonar fusion algorithm used in our navigation system, offering rigorous mathematical formulation of rotation, translation, and calibration transformations to correct for both offset errors and misalignments in sonar sensor directions. The widespread use of the internet facilitates easy communication among users, also enabling easy access to misinformation, particularly fraudulent news gaining significant attention globally since the recent COVID-19 crisis. Our proposed study introduces the utilization of both supervised learning algorithms, specifically Support Vector Machine (SVM), along with the integration of typical text summarization techniques, such as multi-document abstraction, to identify deceptive reports. Notably, researchers have yet to fully explore the connection between known news detection methods and the results of multi-document summary generation. The findings from our experiment using a modified SVM model on the largest available dataset for 5000s reveal that including a parameter that scores the similarity between the text's automatic generated abstracts, which are generated by software, and their corresponding labels from the dataset's construction significantly boosts performance compared to a standard baseline.

This study examines in detail the role of curvature, specifically the mean inner curvature, within Gaussian random fields. We begin by detailing the influence curvature exerts on the distribution of extreme values and subsequently analyze how it facilitates the formation of clusters in these fields, particularly through the lens of percolation and connectivity, to enrich existing theoretical frameworks. Using specific models of gravitational fields as an application case, we offer recommendations for enhancing parameter inference in complex systems.

This work introduces a security framework designed to protect nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) against betrayal by nontrusted users. In this model, a nontrusted user may attempt to decrypt and utilize the decoders of trusted users to execute a side-channel attack on them. Assuming the encoder employs a power allocation strategy based on the channels of all users—and that the nontrusted user has knowledge of these channel states—the security approach relies on analyzing the decoding outcomes at legitimate users to infer their channels secretly. By applying this reasoning, any betrayal can be detected, although it may result in minor fluctuations in data rates for the trusted users within a bounded tolerance. Numerical simulations confirm the proposed method's effectiveness in identifying betrayals and maintaining bounded rate penalties for honest users.

Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global health challenge and is the leading cause of mortality from this fatal disease often begins with benign growths, known as polyps. Microscopic analysis, called dysplasia evaluation, is a key medical procedure used to assess these growths and detect early signs of cancer. However, interpreting these samples is labor-intensive for physicians, leading to significant inter-observer variability in the outcomes. Machine Learning (ML) approaches applied to digital pathology have shown promise in accurately identifying cancer, starting with detecting colorectal polyps. Nevertheless, existing public image datasets lack comprehensive multi-pathologist annotations of dysplasia assessments for colorectal polyps. Therefore, we distributed over two thousand images to one hundred and five researchers in over a hundred countries. In response, we collected five thousand labeled assessments from our participants, resulting in a public dataset known as "UniToPathus." This document describes our protocol, which supplied diverse research community members with identical images to execute an crowdsourced collection of reliable annotations. Finally, we apply various deep neural networks in our paper to demonstrate significant improvements in automatically classifying these colorectal pathologies.

Standard finite element techniques require excessively fine discretizations to accurately model high-frequency scattering problems with smooth coefficients, particularly at "caustics" caused by varying refractive indices or, inacoustically, reflections from coefficients with large gradients. Addressing this limitation utilizing a standard finite element mesh, the current study offers a quantitative analysis of an adaptive algorithm designed specifically for coefficient derivatives, ensuring optimal accuracy under these challenging conditions.

The discovery of the Chelyabinsk meteorite in 2013 provided a chance to study an object from ancient solar system history through careful geological analysis of its trajectory, time evolution, and composition. Our observations indicate that inner solar system planetesimals underwent extensive, dynamic accretion processes roughly 4.56 billion years ago. These findings specifically challenge prevailing models which suggest inner planetesimals formed primarily in dry, low-density (protoplanetary disk midplane) conditions; instead, we found that Chelyabinsk contains abundant water (approximately 2.7–4.4 mass%), with hydrogen and deuterium average ratios in its silicate phase (Si-OD/silicate = $1.4 \pm 0.1 \times 10^{-3}$; D/H = $2.9 \pm 0.4 \times 10^{-4}$) closely resembling those of solar system comets. Since Chelyabinsk forms a rare exposed monolith similar to rare samples like Benenitra, its composition offers direct geological evidence that inner solar system planetesimals accreted water-rich materials in the high-temperature region close to the Sun (temperatures exceeding 450 K), contradicting previous theories that such planetesimals formed dry due to high ambient temperatures near the Sun.

Using the Bethe ansatz, we recently solved a family of XXZ chains with interactions extending up to arbitrary spin $s$. This study reveals how these solvable models evolve as $n$ increases and analyzes their low-energy physics through various analytical methods and numerical checks. Specifically, the exact form factors for these higher-spin systems have been derived. Voice translation (VTC) converts spoken speech across different languages. While translating new languages typically involves tuning on large amounts of parallel data for each language pair, recent advances in end-to-end machine translation allow models to generalize effectively on very small datasets (low VCT can solve problems with very small training sets). This study explores enhancing generalization in speech translation without requiring significant investment in manual data annotation or severe tuning. The paper introduces LowFroS (Zero-phonetic speech translation), which leverages pre-trained models for speech translation and forces the model to use speech inputs by training on small, cleaned, and aligned datasets for unseen language combinations using existing end-to-end techniques. The model achieves superior accuracy compared to standard zero-phonetic methods when evaluated on an eight-language test scenario while using unadjusted, high-quality tools for better results. This study also highlights the value of carefully cleaning and aligning the data for improved outcomes for speech translation.

This paper presents an alternative formulation for multipolar decompositions in electrodynamics, designed to meet current needs within physics and engineering at all length scales. At length scales comparable to or smaller than these applications, traditional theories exhibit limitations. Unlike conventional approaches, this electrodynamical framework organizes induced multipoles according to a rigorous vector spherical harmonic basis, covering both scattering processes and optical influence computations. While these multipoles are not independent at smaller length scales, they enable efficient expansion and numerical methods. Furthermore, at the physical limit of large wavelengths, the formalism recovers standard decomposition types, ensuring consistency with established results.

This study offers a tableau insertion algorithm applicable to algebraic expressions known as double Young-Capelli bitableaux, yielding a tableau expansion for each component of their symmetric algebra basis. These components serve as a universal model for the representations of the pairs of symmetric groups and the quantum general linear group, surpassing existing expansions for Schur altered symmetric functions (the modified version found in the original text). Since these functions serve as alternatives to the well-known Schur functions, their expansion properties are discussed here, along with the difference between them.

This study introduces a simplified scoto-seesaw model that integrates WIMP dark matter (DM) annihilation via pure Higgs portal interactions, leverages new scalar degrees of freedom for a Dirac DM candidate, and generates neutrino masses through the standard scoto-mechanism. We present the leading-order tree diagram phenomenology for both DM annihilation and vacuum stability against the high-energy vacuum meta-stability threshold using next-to-leading-order quantum corrections. Specifically, we identify the model's parameter space capable of simultaneously addressing the DM puzzle, that due to this work the neutrino puzzle, generating correct cosmological abundance of the DM, maintaining stability of the Higgs vacuum; we discuss implications for collider searches and dark matter direct detection experiments as well as constraints from astrophysical considerations within the context of this framework.

This work introduces the notion of relative quantum topological field theory for algebraic stacks equipped with smooth calabi-yau modifications, extending 2d classical Furihi paper field theory with classical (co)homological mappings to incorporate quantum mappings. We examine the behavior these newly defined 2d quantum topological field theories under standard smooth blowups and blowdons, demonstrating smoothly diagonal preservation while demonstrating how to compute the resulting modified mapping for small resolutions of three-factor product varieties' two-factor subvarieties' smooth blowups; specifically showing how to compute these results via the multiplication and blending of constituent maps.

This research presents a supervised approach, enabling the conditioned learning of CXR transformation across various pathologies. By facilitating the specific deformity of anatomical regions associated with certain diseases, this method diversifies corresponding datasets without distorting healthy structures. This creates essential support for optimizing AI performance in disease-specific scenarios. evaluations across seven diagnoses indicate that models trained on these expanded datasets achieve superior or comparable outcomes relative to models trained on undistorted but smaller baseline trials, with improvements in C. Vector fields serve as the primary instrument for visually analyzing physical phenomena ranging from everyday events to complex complex systems. Effectively rendering highly dimensional field data remands visualization (e.g., 4D or 5D) offers only a partial solution, necessitating supplementary filtering or clustering techniques to leverage limited human perceptual capabilities. Existing solutions for organizing and displaying such multidimensional field are nonetheless inadequate, especially when addressing the joint variability of all dimensions. There is a critical need for more capable tools capable of supporting both human perceptual capabilities.

To fill this gap, this paper introduces ViDaExpert, a specialized application designed to visualize and examine high-dimensional velocity fields such as turbulent flow. This system integrates several advanced functionalities—including 3D VoxelViews with advanced rendering, deep-learning driven label propagation, user-driven label refinement, and flexible viewpoint controls—enabling both automatic and user-assisted instance classification. Viewers can now explore flow structures from any angle while clearly perceiving all additional dimensions simultaneously.

Finally, we demonstrate the utility of ViDaExpert by mapping hard-to-perceive flow features within difficult datasets. Our shows that the system can accurately represent intricate structures, even in data sets with up to 5 dimensions where other methods fail or lack full interactivity.

This paper offers a non-domain-specific investigation into the gradient of the Newtonian potential when defined over flat, bounded sets within $\R^d$ for $d\geq 2$. It introduces an equivalent reformulation of $L^p$ boundedness for this operator as a property of the Riesz potential on a function space incorporating domain geometry. This alternative characterization facilitates simpler verifications within various contexts, such as convex domains. Additionally, the work addresses questions regarding unbounded domains by analyzing the operator's behavior in relation to Sobolev functions and its connection to Dirichlet energy.
